title: Vulnerabilities

panels.description: CRITICAL FINDINGS for which a fixed PACKAGE version exists (counted per image and package: the same CVE in two images, or in two packages of one image, counts twice). A fixed package does not mean a newer IMAGE already ships it — see 'Would a version update help?' below.
panels.title: Critical — fix available

panels.description: CRITICAL findings without a fixed package version upstream: nothing to update yet, just be aware (a later image release usually picks the fix up).
panels.title: Critical — no fix yet

panels.description: Number of DIFFERENT CRITICAL CVEs across all running images (with or without fix) — the two tiles on the left count a CVE once per image and package, this is the number of distinct problems behind them.
panels.title: Critical — distinct CVEs

panels.title: High — fix available

panels.description: HIGH findings without a fixed package version upstream: nothing to update yet, just be aware (a later image release usually picks the fix up).
panels.title: High — no fix yet

panels.description: Number of DIFFERENT HIGH CVEs across all running images (with or without fix) — the two tiles on the left count a CVE once per image and package, this is the number of distinct problems behind them.

Would re-pulling help? (same tag, newer build in the registry)

panels.description: Running images whose TAG points to a newer build in the registry (floating tags such as nextcloud:31-apache). 0 = everything is at its tag's current build; pinned version tags normally never change.
panels.title: Images with a newer build

panels.description: Per image with a newer build: CRITICAL findings now minus those in the registry's build (scanned straight from the registry, nothing was redeployed). Empty = no newer builds.
panels.title: CRITICAL a re-pull would remove

targets.expr: sort_desc((sum by (image) (trivy_image_vulnerabilities{severity="CRITICAL"}) - sum by (image) (trivy_image_update_vulnerabilities{severity="CRITICAL"})) and on (image) (trivy_image_update_available == 1))

panels.description: Same for HIGH findings.
panels.title: HIGH a re-pull would remove

targets.expr: sort_desc((sum by (image) (trivy_image_vulnerabilities{severity="HIGH"}) - sum by (image) (trivy_image_update_vulnerabilities{severity="HIGH"})) and on (image) (trivy_image_update_available == 1))

panels.title: Would a version update help? (newer versions scanned straight from the registry)

panels.description: Running images (with an update rule) for which the registry has a newer VERSION tag. same-major = newest within the running major version (the low-risk update); latest = newest overall when that is another major (may skip majors — e.g. Nextcloud must be upgraded one major at a time).
panels.title: Images with a newer version

panels.description: When the comparison with the registries (newer builds + newer versions) last completed. It runs at most once per 12h (in practice: the nightly run) because every run costs registry requests — Docker Hub rate-limits anonymous IPs. Scans in between (button, after an upgrade) reuse the cached result and only rescan the local images; a newly running version gets its update targets from the cached tag lists, its 'after' finding counts follow with the next comparison. Orange after 30h = the registry was unreachable or rate-limited (journalctl -u trivy-metrics).
panels.title: Registry comparison (age)
What an update would change
panels.description: Per running image and update target: CRITICAL/HIGH findings now vs. in the newer version (that version was scanned itself, so this is measured, not guessed). 'after' lower than 'now' = the update removes findings; equal = it does not help (yet).

targets.expr: sum by (update) (label_join(sum by (image) (trivy_image_vulnerabilities{severity="CRITICAL"}) * on (image) group_right() trivy_image_newer_version_info, "update", " | ", "image", "target", "version"))
sum by (update) (label_join(sum by (image) (trivy_image_vulnerabilities{severity="HIGH"}) * on (image) group_right() trivy_image_newer_version_info, "update", " | ", "image", "target", "version"))

panels.description: CRITICAL findings of the running image that are NOT present any more in the newer version (pick the target at the top: same-major or latest). Empty = the update removes no critical finding.
panels.title: Critical CVEs the update would remove (target: $target)

targets.expr: max by (image, cve, pkg, title) ((trivy_vulnerability_info{severity="CRITICAL"} * on (image) group_left() trivy_image_newer_version_info{target="$target"}) unless on (image, cve, pkg) trivy_vulnerability_in_newer{target="$target"})

panels.description: One row per CVE + package: in how many running images it occurs (severity filter at the top; CVSS = score of the source the severity comes from, v4.0 before v3.x; score of the source the severity comes from, CVSS 4.0 before 3.x, 0-10; else the highest any source reports). 'Package fixed in' is the version of the PACKAGE inside the image (e.g. a Debian package) that contains the fix — NOT a version of the application image; empty = no fix yet. Whether a newer image already ships it is not known here. Click a CVE for details. Full list incl. HIGH + titles on the host: /var/lib/trivy-report/vulnerabilities.tsv
panels.title: CVEs across all images

targets.expr: count by (key, cve, rank, pkg, fixed, title) (label_join(trivy_vulnerability_info{severity=~"$severity"}, "key", "|", "cve", "pkg", "fixed"))

panels.description: Every finding of the selected image(s) and severity — pick both with the filters at the top. 'Fixed by' / 'Update to': which update of the IMAGE removes the finding, measured by scanning the newer versions (minor update = newest version of the running major; major update = only the newest version overall; no update yet = still present in every newer version; – = no newer version known for the image). It is the version to update TO, not the first version that fixed it.
panels.title: CVEs per image ($image)

targets.expr: max by (image, cve, rank, fix_target, fix_version, pkg, installed, fixed, title) (trivy_vulnerability_info{image=~"$image",severity=~"$severity"})

panels.description: Fixable findings over time — drops when images are updated, rises when new CVEs are published for what is running.
panels.title: Fixable vulnerabilities over time
Update overview per image
panels.description: Every running image, read left to right. Image age = days since the running image was BUILT: orange from 90, red from 180 days — an image that is no longer rebuilt gets no security fixes (typical for the tag of an end-of-life major version), whatever the CVE counts say. ① Minor update (newest version of the running major): the version to go to and how many CRITICAL/HIGH findings it removes — red = CVSS 9–10, update soon. ② Next major: how many MORE findings only that removes — the realistic next step where majors must not be skipped (Nextcloud). ③ Newest major: what going all the way removes on top. ④ What stays open even then — nothing to do but know. Counts are findings (per package); findings without a CVSS score are in no column. Empty cell = none / no such version. Click a version to upgrade to it from the server itself (opens the confirm page; needs on-host upgrades, roles/local_upgrade).

panels.title: On-host upgrades (last result per service)
panels.description: Upgrades started on the server itself (click a version in the table above, or open the upgrade page). Result: what the upgrade playbook reported — FAILED means it rolled back (details: journalctl -u 'app-upgrade@*' on the host). Empty = none yet, or on-host upgrades are not enabled on this host.
